t: Section 2922a of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(d) The Secretary concerned shall prioritize energy security and resilience.”.

fable.w: The section only directs a federal official (the Secretary concerned) to prioritize energy security and resilience. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no real tempting contrary reading, since no outside actor or participatory process is mentioned.
fable.s: The Secretary concerned shall prioritize energy security and resilience.

opus.w: The amendment only tells a federal official what to prioritize. It does not bring any state, tribe, company, expert or member of the public into a federal decision. Section 2922a is about energy contracts, but entering a contract is not participation. Also, this new text creates no consultation, comment, hearing or right to sue.
opus.s: The Secretary concerned shall prioritize energy security and resilience.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a duty on a federal official (the Secretary) to prioritize certain goals. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). The action is entirely internal to the executive branch.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary concerned shall prioritize energy security and resilience.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "energy security and resilience" implies consulting with external energy providers or experts. However, the text itself contains no requirement for consultation, coordination, or interaction with any outside party. It is a directive to a federal official regarding internal priorities.
